newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon construction declines on yearly basis.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon construction declines on yearly basis.

text.p: Construction picked up slightly in Lebanon in April on a monthly basis but remained below last year's level as the sector continued its downturn trend, the Bank of Lebanon said on Tuesday.
"Construction activity continued its downward trend suffering from market disequilibrium and housing loan scarcity," the bank said in its latest monthly bulletin.
April cement deliveries at 252,000 tonnes were down 1.9 percent on April 1996 but up on March's 233,000 tonnes. March deliveries were 14.1 percent down on a year-on-year basis.
Construction permits approved in April by the Association of Engineers of Beirut and Tripoli totalled 984,118 square metres, a 0.2 percent increase on April 1996, the bank said.
Real estate fees collected totalled 15.6 billion Lebanese pounds, for an annual rise of 15.6 percent.
"During the first four months of the year, real estate fees rose by 13.9 percent from a year earlier," the bank said.
